results.author: Gabe Mills
highlights:
## NVIDIA H100 SXM5 Use Cases, Pricing, and When to Launch 1x or 8x

Gabe Mills, Massed Compute September 2026

Serve a 70B-class model, hold a long context, or train across GPUs that share an NVLink fabric. Massed Compute launches NVIDIA H100 SXM5 for that work as one 80 GB module or as an eight-GPU box. You pick `gpu_1x_H100_SXM5` or `gpu_8x_H100_SXM5` on Deploy. The cards are already in the machine.

A 1x instance is $2.89 an hour as of 16 September 2026. Confirm live 1x and 8x rates on GPU pricing before you launch.

Stay on 1x when weights plus KV still fit 80 GB. Take 8x when you need 16-bit 70B, a cache that spills one card, or tensor parallel across NVLink.

...

This article is H100 SXM5. Hopper SXM, 80 GB HBM3, NVLink on the 8x box. SKUs `gpu_1x_H100_SXM5` and `gpu_8x_H100_SXM5`. The live catalog has no 2x or 4x SXM5.

...

## 1x and 8x shapes

On demand has no contract and no minimum. You pay for the hours you use. Confirm live pricing before you launch.

`gpu_1x_H100_SXM5` is one 80 GB module, 14 vCPU, 122 GiB RAM, and 350 GB disk. `gpu_8x_H100_SXM5` is eight modules (640 GB combined), 126 vCPU, 976 GiB RAM, and 2,800 GB disk.

...

We launched a Massed Compute 1x H100 SXM5 on 10 September 2026. Ubuntu Server 24.04 with NVIDIA drivers. SKU `gpu_1x_H100_SXM5`. Hardware only. No model was served, so this page does not invent 1x tok/s.

...

$2.89 on demand with no contract, current as of 16 September 2026. Confirm live 1x and 8x rates on GPU pricing before you launch.

### What GPU type do I pick on Deploy?

H100 SXM5 (80GB). Then pick quantity ×1 or ×8. That maps to `gpu_1x_H100_SXM5` and `gpu_8x_H100_SXM5`.

Is PowerGPU cheaper than Massed Compute?

On most overlapping cards, yes: Massed Compute lists the H100 SXM5 at $2.89/hr and the A100 80 GB at $1.35-1.38/hr on its public pricing page (checked 2026-09-04); PowerGPU fixes both at the public market median × 0.70. results.title: Flopper Now Tracks GPU Rental Prices Across 24 Cloud Providers | Flopper.io
highlights:
337 per-GPU hourly rates from 24 clouds, refreshed every six hours, with price history back to July 2026. The spec database now tells you what each accelerator costs to rent, and who is cheapest today.

Published September 9, 2026 · Flopper.io Research

Flopper.io started as a specification database: peak TFLOPS by precision, memory, bandwidth and power for every datacenter GPU. Specs answer half of the buying question. The other half is price, and that number lives on 24 different pricing pages, in 24 different units. As of today, the pricing index collects 337 live listings from 24 GPU cloud providers, covering 89 GPUs, normalized to one unit: US dollars per GPU per hour. The pipeline refreshes every six hours and has recorded every price change since 14 July 2026, so each GPU page now carries a price history alongside its spec sheet.

## What the Same GPU Costs, Cloud to Cloud

The spread is the story. On the day of publication, an on-demand H100 SXM5 80 GB (2022) is listed by 16 providers, and the most expensive listing costs nearly seven times the cheapest. The B200 (2024) shows the same pattern with a three-fold gap across eight clouds. Some of that gap is real: interconnect, storage, support and region all cost money. Some of it is simply price discovery that has not happened yet, because nobody was lining the numbers up.

No two providers quote the same way. One prices an eight-GPU node, another a single accelerator, a third a monthly contract, and Scaleway prices in euros. Every listing goes through the same four steps before it reaches a page.

- Per GPU, per hour, in USD. Node prices are divided by the GPU count. Monthly rates are divided by 730 hours. Non-USD prices are converted at the live exchange rate on the day of the sync.
- Pricing types are kept apart. On-demand (191 listings), spot or preemptible (31), marketplace community hosts (111) and reserved commitments (4) never share a row. The headline cheapest price on each GPU page is always on-demand, so an interruptible instance cannot masquerade as the market rate.
- Every listing maps to one canonical part. A provider's "H100" is matched to the exact variant it sells, SXM5 or PCIe, 80 GB or 94 GB, so a PCIe price never dilutes the SXM figure. Names the matcher cannot place are logged and dropped rather than guessed.
- Bad data is quarantined, not published. A listing that lands far outside its GPU's price band is held back and flagged for review. Median, dispersion and FP8-per-dollar figures on the pricing index are calculated so that a single bad listing cannot move them.

...

A price comparison that only shows today cannot tell you whether $2.99 for an H200 is a bargain or the new normal. Since 14 July 2026 the pipeline has recorded 2,297 price points across 58 days and 101 GPUs, appending a row every time a listing changes. Each GPU pricing page plots the last 30 days with one line per provider, so you can see who cut, who held, and who quietly raised.

...

That figure compares the same providers' listings at both ends of the window, so a new cloud joining coverage registers as more data, not as a price move.

The aggregate figure at the top of the table is a simple average of the 1-GPU on-demand prices available that day — not weighted by usage, and it can move when a GPU is added to or dropped from the comparison, not only when a price changes. results.title: Cheapest A100 Rental: 40GB vs 80GB Prices by Provider · Aliteq
results.author: Aliteq Team
highlights:
On Nov 12, 2026 a 40GB A100 rented from $0.32/hr on Vast.ai and an 80GB one from $0.81/hr (Lium; Vast from $0.84), against $1.35 on Hyperstack (Nov 3) and $1.79 on Runpod. Where the cheap A100s are, why 80GB costs about twice as much, and the jobs that need it.

...

The cheapest A100 rental is on Vast.ai's marketplace, and the memory size changes the price. In our read of Vast's offer API at 13:30 UTC on Nov 3, 2026, a 40GB A100 started at $0.40/hour on-demand (median $0.53 across 39 offers) and an 80GB A100 at $0.63/hour (median $1.00 across 25 offers). The cheapest 80GB card from a Vast-verified host was $1.00. Managed 80GB A100s listed at $1.35 on Hyperstack and $1.79 on Runpod Secure Cloud. Pay for 80GB when you run a 70B model, gpt-oss-120b or a 70B fine-tune; for 32B-class models and smaller fine-tunes, 40GB does the job for about half the price. Prices move every hour, so check today's live prices before you rent.

...

The cheapest A100 rental on November 3, 2026 was on Vast.ai's marketplace: an A100 40GB from $0.40 an hour on-demand (median $0.53) and an A100 80GB from $0.63 an hour (median $1.00 across 25 offers; the cheapest from a verified host was $1.00). Managed 80GB A100s listed at $1.35 an hour on Hyperstack and $1.79 on Runpod Secure Cloud. Lambda and CoreWeave sell 80GB A100s only in 8-GPU machines, at $2.79 and $2.70 per GPU-hour. The 80GB card is worth its roughly double price when the job needs more than 40GB: Llama 3.3 70B at 4-bit (about 43 GB at 8K context by our estimate), gpt-oss-120b (OpenAI says it runs on a single 80GB GPU), QLoRA fine-tuning of a 70B model (41 GB per Unsloth) or 16-bit LoRA of a 32B model (76 GB). For 32B models at 8-bit with short context, or QLoRA up to about 40B, a 40GB A100 is enough.

...

Our Nov 12 pull of Vast's offer API (18:04 UTC, 56 rentable A100 offers split by memory size): a 40GB A100 from $0.32 an hour on-demand (median $0.60 across 41 offers; verified hosts from $0.40) and an 80GB A100 from $0.84 (median $0.87 across 15 offers; verified hosts from $1.02). Interruptible 80GB bids started at $0.18. In our hourly feed (17:20 UTC), Lium listed an A100 80GB PCIe at $0.81 and Runpod Secure Cloud was unchanged at $1.79 for either 80GB version. Fewer cheap 80GB offers than on Nov 3, so the 80GB floor rose from $0.63 to $0.81-0.84. The other providers' rates below were read on Nov 3 and not re-read.

Every day at 00:05 UTC the index records, for each of the 13 GPUs in the basket, the minimum, median and maximum price per GPU-hour across every current offer on the site. An offer is current only when all of the following hold:

- the provider reports it as available right now;
- the provider has live stock tracking, so "available" is a real-time observation, not a catalog entry;
- it was seen within the last 15 minutes;
- it is secure on-demand pricing on provider-operated data-center hardware, billed per GPU-hour;
- spot, interruptible, reserved and peer-to-peer or marketplace listings are excluded.

# NVIDIA A100

Ampere · 80 GB
